papers.title: An embryo-derived peptide signal directs endosperm polarity in Arabidopsis.
papers.summary: In Arabidopsis, the receptor kinase IKU2 with transcription factor WRKY10/MINISEED3 establishes endosperm polarity through homeodomain factors WOX8 and WOX9. The process requires egg-cell fertilization and is mediated by the embryo-derived peptide PIPL7, a potential IKU2 ligand, revealing an embryo-to-endosperm paracrine dialog that coordinates seed development.

papers.title: Thalamic NRXN1-mediated input to human cortical progenitors drives excitatory neurogenesis.
papers.summary: Fusing human cortical and thalamic organoids shows thalamic input increases cortical excitatory neuron production. Neurexin-1 (NRXN1) mediates physical contact between thalamic axons and cortical outer radial glia; thalamic NRXN1 knockout reduces these contacts and attenuates upper-layer excitatory neurogenesis, revealing how thalamic projections shape early human cortical development.

papers.title: Early-life colonization with Clostridioides difficile remodels the developing gut.
papers.summary: In neonatal mice, Clostridioides difficile colonization drives proinflammatory and repair responses in gut epithelium, expanding injury-associated stem cells and skewing secretory differentiation, with persistent adult changes. Effects are toxin-dependent: nontoxigenic strains and maternal mRNA-LNP vaccination protect neonates, and colonized human infants show altered intestinal stem-cell behavior.

papers.title: Tumor-derived antioxidants suppress immunity by depriving T cells of reactive oxygen species.
papers.summary: Tumors release the antioxidant enzyme peroxiredoxin 1 (PRDX1) into their interstitial fluid, depriving T cells of reactive oxygen species needed for TCR-driven kinase signaling. PRDX1 rises during cancer immunoediting; its loss in tumors enhances antitumor immunity and immunotherapy responses, defining a redox-based immunosuppression mechanism.

papers.title: Yellow protein co-opted to sustain obligate symbiosis in leaf beetles.
papers.summary: A female-specific yellow protein in tortoise beetles forms gelatinous spheres that encapsulate the bacterium Stammera during vertical transmission, protecting the reduced-genome symbiont outside the body. Expressed in symbiont-harboring ovary glands, yellow knockdown disrupts sphere integrity and symbiont viability, revealing co-option of an ancient insect gene family for symbiosis.

papers.title: Heat shock-induced autophagy has cargo selectivity in Saccharomyces cerevisiae.
papers.summary: Heat shock in Saccharomyces cerevisiae triggers autophagic degradation of ubiquitinated protein aggregates via the macroaggrephagy receptor Cue5. Heat stress also induces turnover of the aggrephagy receptor Cct2 and polyglutamine huntingtin fragments; this vacuole-dependent degradation proceeds independently of canonical autophagy pathways, establishing a proteostasis role for autophagy after heat stress.

papers.title: Guanine promotes acute lung injury by repressing H3K27me3 in sepsis.
papers.summary: During sepsis, peripheral-blood macrophages secrete exosomal G6PD, which rewires purine metabolism: accumulated guanine reduces H3K27me3 by suppressing EZH2 synthesis, inducing Nos2, Ccl6, and Il6 and causing acute lung injury. Rab27a or G6PD knockout protects mice, and G6PD inhibitors or si-G6PD-engineered vesicles relieve injury.

papers.title: Mutation accumulation in a hybrid parthenogenetic vertebrate.
papers.summary: In the hybrid parthenogenetic whiptail lizard Aspidoscelis tesselatus, both parental subgenomes show elevated nonsynonymous substitution ratios and expressed-transcript indels predicted to disrupt protein domains, affecting chromatin organization, apoptosis, and transcription genes. The maternal subgenome carries more mutations, supporting Muller's ratchet as a driver of mutation accumulation in asexual vertebrates.

papers.title: Local lactate-driven H3K18 lactylation impairs anti-influenza immunity through NRF2-dependent dendritic cell dysfunction.
papers.summary: Influenza infection elevates lung lactate, which enters dendritic cells via monocarboxylate transporters and induces a tolerogenic state with impaired maturation and reduced CD8 T-cell priming. Lactate-driven H3K18 histone lactylation links to enhancer accessibility and NRF2 activation, and NRF2 reinforces dendritic-cell suppression during antiviral immunity.

papers.title: Membrane engagement by the HLA-A cytoplasmic tail regulates endocytosis and surface retention.
papers.summary: The HLA-A cytoplasmic tail contains a conserved membrane-responsive segment (residues 360-365) that engages phospholipids and undergoes Cys363-dependent self-association. Disrupting this segment weakens ARF6 association, slows receptor internalization, and prolongs surface HLA-A retention; a cell-penetrating peptide of this sequence limits MHC-I loss from tumor cells.

papers.title: Engineering the insulin signal peptide to protect human pancreatic beta cells from autoimmune destruction.
papers.summary: Replacing insulin's signal peptide with chromogranin-A's in human beta cells lacking endogenous insulin preserves insulin synthesis, processing, secretion, and activity while allowing cells to evade recognition and killing by autoreactive T cells, without inducing ER stress or altering cell identity - an alternative to HLA knockout for stem-cell-derived diabetes therapy.

papers.title: Multiscale physical effects of CpG methylation on DNA mechanics, nucleosome wrapping, and chromatin condensates.
papers.summary: Using single-molecule force spectroscopy, FRAP, and nanorheology, CpG methylation modestly stiffens DNA and weakens nucleosome wrapping, while methylated chromatin condensates show reduced internal mobility and increased viscoelasticity. Methylation cooperates with H3K9me3 in HP1alpha-mediated condensation without changing HP1alpha-DNA affinity, supporting a multiscale physical model of heterochromatin formation.

papers.title: Cr(VI) and DON co-exposure triggers intestinal epithelial cells ferroptosis and pyroptosis through Nrf2/NF-κB/NLRP3 to impair intestinal barrier function.
papers.journal: Redox report : communications in free radical research
papers.summary: Co-exposure to chromium(VI) and deoxynivalenol disrupts intestinal tight junctions in broiler epithelial cells by inducing oxidative stress, inhibiting Nrf2, and abnormally activating NF-kB/NLRP3, triggering ferroptosis and pyroptosis. Nrf2 overexpression or NLRP3/NF-kB silencing reverses iron accumulation, inflammatory cytokine secretion, and barrier dysfunction bidirectionally.

papers.title: OsDUF1223 negatively regulates seedling drought tolerance and modulates nitrate-dependent root growth in rice.
papers.summary: The plasma membrane protein OsDUF1223 acts as a negative regulator of drought tolerance in rice seedlings: overexpressing lines show lower survival, higher water loss, and reduced antioxidant activity and osmolyte accumulation. Transcriptomic and physiological analyses link OsDUF1223 to ABA signaling and nitrogen response pathways, offering a breeding candidate.

papers.title: Effective Tumor Protection by a Tumor-Associated Mucin-1 Glycopeptide-Based Conjugate Vaccine in a Spontaneous Mouse Breast Cancer Model.
papers.summary: A tumor-associated MUC1 glycopeptide (Thomsen-nouveau antigen) conjugated to bacteriophage Qbeta was tested in spontaneous MUC1-transgenic breast cancer mice. The vaccine induced high anti-TMUC1 IgG selective for glycan and peptide, antibodies bound tumor cells and killed via complement, and 83 percent of treated mice outlived controls.

papers.title: Promiscuous Metal Site in Hepatitis B Virus X Protein Binds an Fe-S Cluster.
papers.summary: Chemoproteomics and HyScore spectroscopy identify hepatitis B virus X protein as an Fe-S cluster-binding protein: cysteines C61, C69, C143, and C148 coordinate the cluster, with C137 auxiliary, and histidine coordination is excluded. These residues support Zn binding, overlap transactivation regions, and HBX engages the host Fe-S assembly machinery.

papers.title: Linker Histone H1 Phosphorylation Promotes DNA Damage Repair during Replication Stress.
papers.summary: The S-phase-phosphorylated form of linker histone H1 promotes DNA damage repair at collapsed replication forks. Phosphorylation enhances H1 assembly on single-stranded DNA, and phospho-H1 engages replication and damage-response factors including HPF1, promoting liquid-like assemblies associated with reduced DNA damage and histone PARylation; H1 depletion increases damage sensitivity.

papers.title: Sialotranscriptome of Simulium pertinax and functional characterization of SpVaP: a novel recombinant simuliid-specific vasodilator.
papers.summary: Transcriptomic analysis of Simulium pertinax (black fly) salivary glands identified 15,708 transcripts including 1,947 secreted-protein clusters across 23 families. The black fly-restricted SVEP family was highly represented; a recombinant member, SpVaP, elicited vasodilation in mouse arterioles and paw edema, revealing a novel vasoactive blood-feeding protein.

papers.title: Emerging Paradigms in Glycobiology.
papers.summary: This historical review describes how classical glycobiology paradigms - glycosylation limited to secreted and membrane proteins, nonspecific low-affinity glycan binding, and random glycosylation - were overturned. Emerging paradigms include widespread amino-acid glycosylation, site-specific glycosylation, glycoproteins in all cellular compartments, and central glycan roles in human disease.

papers.title: HNRNPC contributes to ccRCC progression by stabilizing AURKB mRNA in an m6A-dependent manner.
papers.summary: HNRNPC is overexpressed in clear cell renal cell carcinoma and stabilizes AURKB mRNA by binding m6A sites, promoting proliferation, sphere formation, migration, and invasion. Knockdown of HNRNPC or AURKB suppresses xenograft growth and Ki-67, suggesting the HNRNPC/AURKB axis as a therapeutic target in ccRCC.

papers.title: Memory of growth promotes early Ras GTPase activation to establish dominance of inherited cell ends in S. pombe.
papers.summary: In fission yeast, inherited Rax1/2 proteins mark the previously growing cell end and promote early Ras1-GTPase activation by recruiting the GEF Efc25, enabling timely Cdc42 transition to the old end. This growth memory establishes old-end dominance; altering Ras1 regulators correspondingly changes inherited-end growth advantage.

papers.title: Sex-specific control of locomotor behavior by neuronal Arhgef10 in aged Drosophila.
papers.summary: Drosophila Arhgef10 knockout flies show abnormal walking kinematics that worsen with age, especially in females. Effects arise mainly from neuronal requirement: females are sensitive to total Arhgef10 loss with reduced wakefulness and speed, while males are affected by isoform imbalance; motor-neuron knockdown disrupts adult muscle innervation.

papers.title: Dissecting contributions of directional and balancing selection to trajectories of mitochondrial haplotype evolution in Drosophila melanogaster.
papers.journal: Evolution; international journal of organic evolution
papers.summary: Experimental evolution of Drosophila mitochondrial haplotypes across temperatures and starting frequencies shows haplotype trajectories shaped by temperature, frequency dependence, and nuclear background. Contrary to simple thermal-adaptation predictions, haplotype a1 was favored at both temperatures; simulations support directional selection only in some backgrounds, otherwise negative frequency-dependent balancing selection with mito-nuclear epistasis.

papers.title: Chromosome-Level Reference Genome of the Desert Night Lizard Xantusia vigilis.
papers.summary: Using PacBio long-read, Hi-C, and RNA-seq data, researchers assembled a reference-quality 2.2 Gb genome for the desert night lizard Xantusia vigilis with 20 scaffolds matching the karyotype and a complete mitochondrion. Chromosome 1 aligns to both macrochromosome 1 and microchromosome 9 of a cordylid relative, indicating fused ancestry.

papers.title: Liver organoids: modelling complexity in homeostasis and disease.
papers.summary: This review covers liver organoid advances in modeling hepatocyte complexity, maturation, and architecture in vitro, including applications to genetic and metabolic liver diseases and liver cancer. It discusses current limitations relative to 2D lines and whole animals, and provides a perspective on improving organoid models for liver biology.

papers.title: Rapid derivation of cloning-competent cells from peripheral blood advances conservation biobanking.
papers.summary: Endothelial progenitor cells and pericytes from peripheral blood provide alternatives to skin fibroblasts for conservation biobanking: canid blood-derived cells double 2-3 fold faster, reach bankable lines in 1.5-2 weeks, show genomic stability, and generate viable embryos via interspecific nuclear transfer; gray wolf cells yielded six fetuses after transfer.

papers.title: Long-term rock dove (Columba livia) primordial germ cell culture: A tool towards avian conservation.
papers.summary: Researchers derived and long-term cultured primordial germ cells from rock doves using a species-specific medium. Insulin signaling was required for survival; retinoic acid receptor inhibition with vitamin A supported propagation, and BMP4, LIF, GDNF, and pleiotrophin enhanced proliferation. Cultured cells expressed germline markers and migrated to gonads in embryos.

papers.title: Inducing radiation resilience in frozen animal cells via mRNA coding for tardigrade damage-suppressor protein in support of space travel and Lunar storage.
papers.summary: This review proposes protecting cryopreserved animal fibroblasts in a lunar biorepository from long-term radiation by delivering modified mRNA encoding the tardigrade damage-suppressor protein via nanoparticles, minimizing DNA damage without genomic modification or apparent toxicity. The approach could also serve as a testbed for radiation countermeasures during long-duration human spaceflight.

papers.title: Polygenic and monogenic adaptation drive evolutionary rescue at different magnitudes of environmental change.
papers.summary: Forward-in-time simulations seeded with Arabidopsis thaliana genomic variation show polygenic architectures increase evolutionary rescue under small-to-moderate environmental change but predictably fail under extreme shifts, where monogenic traits occasionally produce winning adaptive genotypes. Polygenic architectures yield stable fitness variance while monogenic ones produce skewed outcomes, informing conservation and assisted adaptation strategies.

papers.title: Genomic erosion in the assessment of species' extinction risk and recovery potential.
papers.summary: This perspective defines genomic erosion - loss of diversity, deleterious mutation accumulation, maladaptation, and introgression - and its time-lagged 'drift debt' persisting after demographic recovery. Simulations show how ancestral population size and bottlenecks shape genetic load, and present a proof-of-concept genomic framework aligning metrics with IUCN green status assessments.

papers.title: The value of structural variants to conservation genomics in the pangenome era.
papers.summary: This review argues structural variants - insertions, deletions, inversions, transpositions - are a major but underused axis of diversity for conservation genomics, affecting phenotype, local adaptation, and inbreeding genetic load. Population-scale long-read sequencing and pangenome approaches are making SV detection and analysis feasible for conservation management of small populations.

papers.title: Ex situ reared black-footed ferrets exhibit altered sperm DNA methylation.
papers.summary: Comparing 12 ex situ and 5 in situ black-footed ferret males, sperm from captive-reared animals showed significantly higher DNA methylation and over 500 differentially methylated regions enriched for reproduction and development genes, including spermatogenesis and fertilization genes, suggesting epigenetic mechanisms underlie reduced reproductive success of ex situ populations.

papers.title: A chromosome-level genome of the Nicobar pigeon, Caloenas nicobarica.
papers.summary: A haplotype-resolved, chromosome-level genome of the Nicobar pigeon - the dodo's closest living relative - was assembled with PacBio HiFi and Hi-C, each haplotype spanning about 1.2 Gb with high contiguity. This first high-quality assembly of an Indo-Pacific columbid supports phylogenetic, adaptation, and conservation studies.

papers.title: OligoSeq: Rapid nanopore-sequencing of single-stranded oligonucleotides.
papers.summary: OligoSeq combines AmpliSeq (PCR-based) and RevSeq (reverse-complementation) methods to enable rapid nanopore sequencing of single-stranded oligonucleotides, resolving reference sequences via anchor matches and basecall frequencies. It offers cost-effective quality control for oligo synthesis, gene-expression libraries, and DNA data storage compared to Illumina, PacBio, or HPLC/MS approaches.

papers.title: Multidimensional nutritional assessment in Crohn's disease: Cross-sectional comparison of active disease and remission.
papers.summary: Among 127 Bangladeshi adults with Crohn's disease, 47 percent met GLIM malnutrition criteria, with far higher rates in active disease than remission (81 vs 14 percent). Active disease showed lower anthropometric measures, hemoglobin, iron, albumin, and zinc, supporting multidimensional nutritional assessment combining anthropometry with targeted biochemistry.

papers.title: EIF1 coordinates transcriptomic and splicing networks associated with cell cycle dysregulation in diabetic retinopathy.
papers.summary: In an ARPE-19 hyperglycemia model of diabetic retinopathy, the RNA-binding protein EIF1 was downregulated. EIF1 knockdown altered 223 genes and 1,211 alternative splicing events, notably in cell cycle and p53 pathways including BIRC5, MCM4, PLK1, and COP1/TFE3 splicing, RT-qPCR validated, implicating EIF1 in retinal cell-cycle dysregulation.

papers.title: Comprehensive analysis of non-synonymous single-nucleotide polymorphism of human TSC1 and TSC2 genes: An in silico approach.
papers.summary: Using twelve computational tools with ROC analysis, structural modeling, and molecular dynamics, researchers identified twelve high-risk nonsynonymous SNPs in TSC1 and sixteen in TSC2 that reduce protein stability, occur in conserved regions, and potentially disrupt phosphorylation sites, including variants affecting TSC1 local folding and TSC2 RHEB binding.

papers.title: The G-patch protein Cwf28 interacts with the RNA helicase Cdc28 in catalytically active spliceosomes in Schizosaccharomyces pombe.
papers.summary: Tandem affinity purification and mass spectrometry place the essential G-patch protein Cwf28 within catalytically active Schizosaccharomyces pombe spliceosomes, associated with the PRP19 complex. Cwf28's most abundant interactor is the DEAH-box RNA helicase Cdc28 (human DHX16 ortholog), and their interaction requires Cwf28's conserved G-patch domain.

papers.title: ILF3 regulates erythroid differentiation: A single-cell transcriptomic analysis and cellular experiment.
papers.summary: Single-cell transcriptomics of beta-thalassemia shows ILF3 downregulated throughout erythroid differentiation, with ILF3-positive cells enriched for maturation genes and cell-cycle pathways while ILF3-negative cells express stress genes and inflammatory programs. ILF3 knockout in K562 cells promotes apoptosis, linking ILF3 deficiency to erythroid differentiation arrest in thalassemia.

papers.title: Molecular docking, molecular dynamics simulation, and enzyme inhibitory studies of vitamin K family members on aldose reductase.
papers.summary: Combining molecular docking, dynamics simulations, MM/GBSA energetics, and enzyme kinetics, vitamin K2 showed the strongest aldose reductase binding, stabilized mainly by hydrophobic contacts, with K1 slightly weaker and K3 unstable in the active site. Vitamin K1 and K2 emerge as promising natural aldose reductase inhibitors for diabetic complications.

papers.title: Oocyte quality in endometriosis-associated infertility: a narrative analysis of mechanisms and therapeutic options.
papers.summary: This narrative review links endometriosis-associated infertility to oocyte quality: a hostile follicular microenvironment of inflammation, oxidative stress, and granulosa dysfunction causes spindle disorders, mitochondrial DNA damage, and delayed maturation. Because good-quality embryos achieve normal implantation, the defect is oocyte-driven; therapy combines lifestyle modification and individualized assisted reproduction.

papers.title: Desmoplakin loss in alveolar epithelium drives Wnt/β-Catenin-mediated extracellular matrix remodeling and fibrotic signaling in vitro.
papers.summary: Silencing desmoplakin in A549 alveolar epithelial cells induces epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition, migration, and permeability while destabilizing plakoglobin, reducing beta-catenin turnover, and activating TCF/LEF transcription of fibrotic genes including COL1A1 and MMP9. Desmoplakin overexpression or Wnt pathway inhibition suppresses these effects, implicating dysplakin loss in fibrotic ECM remodeling.

papers.title: Cytotoxic and molecular effects of S-allylcysteine on uterine leiomyoma primary culture cells.
papers.summary: S-allylcysteine from aged garlic reduced primary uterine leiomyoma cell viability dose-dependently (IC50 about 256 micrograms/ml) with apoptotic morphology, while adjacent myometrial cells were less sensitive. Treated fibroid cells showed downregulated PI3K, AKT3, and MTOR transcripts and upregulated PTEN, supporting S-allylcysteine as a potential leiomyoma therapeutic.

papers.title: Recent advancements in exosomal content analysis: the future of liquid biopsy.
papers.summary: This review surveys exosome cargo analysis for liquid biopsy: proteomics yields scalable diagnostic protein signatures and RNA sequencing profiles transcriptomes, with exosomal biomarkers advancing neurological, infectious, cardiovascular, and oncology diagnostics. Remaining barriers include nonstandardized isolation, variable yield and purity, biological heterogeneity, and limited large-scale clinical validation.

papers.title: Remodeling-phase wound-derived protein factors enhance mesenchymal stem cell function and improve diabetic wound healing.
papers.summary: Conditioning mesenchymal stem cells with remodeling-phase wound factors from normal day-9 rat wounds enhanced scratch closure, restored tissue architecture, improved collagen organization, and increased alpha-SMA-positive vasculature in diabetic wounds, whereas diabetic wound extract conditioning raised inflammatory genes, showing phase-specific wound cues can optimize stem-cell therapy for diabetic wounds.

papers.title: Whole-genome analysis of Brevibacterium sanguinis AZMABM HM27: a bacterial isolate from the sea anemone Radianthus magnifica and exhibiting promising multi-therapeutic properties.
papers.summary: Whole-genome analysis of Brevibacterium sanguinis AZMABM HM27, isolated from the sea anemone Radianthus magnifica, reveals a 3.83 Mb chromosome with 95 secondary-metabolite genes and five biosynthetic clusters including ectoine, terpene, and siderophore pathways. Crude extracts showed antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, antidiabetic, and antiproliferative activities against MCF-7 breast cancer cells.

papers.title: Neem leaf glycoprotein mediated immunomodulation and epigenetic regulation in Acute Myeloid Leukemia.
papers.summary: Neem leaf glycoprotein enhanced lymphocyte proliferation, TH1 cytokine secretion, and activation in healthy and acute myeloid leukemia immune cells. Chromatin immunoprecipitation showed increased H3K4me3, H3K14ac, and p53 with reduced H3K27me3, HDAC1, Notch1, and c-Myc at IFNG/TBX21 loci, and cytotoxic T cells killed AML cells more effectively.

papers.title: BNIP3/NIX-dependent mitophagy: molecular mechanisms and physiological roles.
papers.summary: This review summarizes BNIP3/NIX-dependent mitophagy: how these receptors are transcriptionally induced and post-translationally regulated, how they couple to the core autophagy machinery, and their roles in isolation-membrane tethering, elongation, and mitophagosome formation, particularly under hypoxic and metabolic stress, contributing to mitochondrial homeostasis, redox balance, and stress adaptation.

papers.title: Involvement of the OB-fold and the C-terminal acidic tip of SSB in its interaction with RecO from Thermus thermophilus HB8.
papers.summary: Using domain-truncated SSB variants from Thermus thermophilus, RecO was shown to bind both the SSB OB-fold and the C-terminal acidic tip. Arg127 in RecO recognizes the C-tip and contributes to dsDNA binding; the C-tip modulates SSB dynamics on ssDNA, and stable SSB-RecO-RecR assembly requires it.

papers.title: Structure and biochemical analyses suggest that PrkA/YeaG protein of Thermus thermophilus functions as a putative molecular chaperone.
papers.summary: Cryo-EM structures of the Thermus thermophilus PrkA/YeaG homolog TpkB reveal a hexameric AAA+ ring with N-terminal, ATPase, and lid domains. TpkB shows ATPase and chaperone-like activities but no protein kinase activity, structurally resembling MOXR family proteins linked to von Willebrand factor A domain partners, redefining this kinase family.

papers.title: RNA structural biology of neurodegeneration: phase separation, phase transition and proteinopathy.
papers.summary: This review examines how RNA structures regulate phase behavior of prion-like proteins in neurodegeneration: RNA promotes liquid-liquid phase separation and subsequent sol-gel transitions, with RNA G-quadruplexes emerging as pathological determinants driving aberrant phase transition, aggregation, and proteinopathy in Alzheimer's and Parkinson's disease.

papers.title: Development and validation of a novel monocyte activation test with secreted luciferase-expressing cells.
papers.summary: A monocyte activation test using Mono-Mac-6 cells engineered with an NF-kB-driven secreted NanoLuc reporter detects endotoxin within 3 hours and maintains stable signal 3-12 hours, recognizes multiple pyrogens including flagellin and peptidoglycan, and, with lipopolysaccharide-binding protein, enables serum-free testing - an improved alternative to donor-variable whole-blood tests.

papers.title: Substrate specificity of an archaeal thioesterase from Thermococcus kodakarensis.
papers.summary: TK1652 from Thermococcus kodakarensis is the first characterized archaeal thioesterase: a hotdog-fold homodimer with acetyl-CoA activity but negligible activity toward the acyl-CoA substrates of TE8/TE13 enzymes, which are tetrameric. Distinct active-site residues, quaternary structure, and specificity define a new thioesterase family, with activity confirmed in cell-free extracts.
